docs.title: KUMA User Guide
docs.text:
KUMA is a desktop app for site-directed mutagenesis campaigns. KURO designs SDM primer pairs in batch from a Gibson Assembly template. MAME reads the Oxford Nanopore sequencing that comes back and tells which clones carry the intended mutation.

Kuro output step with the bundled demo project, captured from an earlier build.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Download the installer for your system from Releases.

System File Windows (x64) kuma_<version>_x64-setup.exe macOS (Apple Silicon) kuma_<version>_aarch64.dmg Linux (x64) kuma_<version>_amd64.AppImage or kuma_<version>_amd64.deb

On first launch KUMA asks for a projects folder (default ~/Documents/kuma). macOS shows an unidentified-developer warning the first time; the README lists the two ways past it.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• KURO guide: from loading a sequence to the primer order sheet and liquid-handler files.
  • MAME guide: from a MinKNOW run folder to verdicts and EVOLVEpro input.

These are the same pages the app shows in its help panel, so the guide and the app describe the same version.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Common questions about KURO and MAME. Each answer names the screen where the setting or the message lives.

docs.title: My FASTA file isn't accepted on Step 1
docs.text: KURO designs from the CDS annotation, and a FASTA file carries none. The screen says CDS annotation required. Use a GenBank (.gb/.gbk) or SnapGene (.dna) file. Load a GenBank or SnapGene file instead. See Step 1. Load Variants.

docs.title: Why does the design count stop at 96?
docs.text: One design run covers one plate. A larger value is set back to 96 with Design count limited to one plate of variants. See Step 3. Primer Parameters.

docs.title: Picking a polymerase changed my Tm and GC values
docs.text: Picking a preset overwrites the Tm targets and the GC range with that preset's values. Check them again if you'd set them by hand. See Step 3. Primer Parameters.

docs.title: Run Design says Sidecar is not ready
docs.text: Use the Retry button in the status bar, or restart the app. See Step 4. Pool Filters & Run.

docs.title: The Summary table reads This workspace has no primer results
docs.text: A design input changed after the run, so the primer output was discarded. The message gives the time and the counts. Run the design again on Step 4. See Step 5. Summary.

docs.title: Export stays disabled with wells exceed one 96-well plate.
docs.text: Clear Include on rows in the Summary table until 96 or fewer remain. See Step 6. Export.

docs.title: Which KURO file does MAME need?
docs.text: The plate map ..._platemap.xlsx, which every export writes. Open the MAME tab from the same project folder when the sequencing data come back.

docs.title: Do I have to sort the reads by barcode first?
docs.text: No. Give step 2 the MinKNOW run folder as it is. MAME reads the .fastq and .fastq.gz files under fastq_pass/ and splits the barcodes itself. See Step 2. Sequencing Review.

docs.title: The run finished with no verdicts at all
docs.text:
The Analysis finished with 0 wells dialog opens and lists how many reads were dropped at each stage. Read these two counts first.

  • Reads passing MAPQ is 0: no read aligned to the reference. Check that the reference file is the construct that was actually sequenced.
  • Reads passing coverage is 0: reads aligned but none covered enough of the reference. A whole-construct reference used against amplicon reads looks like this. Use the amplicon region as the reference, or lower Coverage Fraction under Advanced options.

The dialog also asks you to check that the expected mutations file covers the variants in this run, and that the selected folder is the right run with reads in its barcode folders.

docs.title: A notice says the coverage gate discarded a share of the aligned reads
docs.text: Some loss is expected, because partial and chimeric reads are meant to be dropped. Wells that lose every read get no verdict, so on screen they look the same as wells the bench never filled. A large share points at the reference rather than the samples. An alignment that stops a fixed number of bases short of the reference ends, at a primer for instance, fails the percentage threshold more easily when the amplicon is short. Coverage Fraction is under Advanced options in step 2.1.

docs.title: Why didn't amplicon extraction happen?
docs.text: The primer sites are absent from the reference, match several positions, or appear in reversed order. A reference holding only the CDS has the primers outside it, so absence is normal there. When extraction is skipped and even the longest read can't clear the coverage requirement, the run is refused before it starts.

docs.title: A mutation is named as sitting at a reference end
docs.text: In a run aligned against the reference as supplied, an expected mutation within 30 bp of either end is named above the verdict table. The aligner clips reads at that point, so the position can be read shallower than the depth the well reports. A reference that includes the primer binding regions puts the mutation further inside.

docs.title: The screen says plate folders were produced by an earlier run
docs.text: Those folders sit in the output folder but don't belong to the run recorded there, so they were left out of the verdicts. Nothing was deleted. Check whether you still want them before removing them yourself, and use a separate output folder for each run.

docs.title: The pore count is blank
docs.text: report_*.json wasn't found in the run folder or one level up. Blank means not read, not zero. No pass line is set on pore counts either way.

docs.title: Do I have to do step 3?
docs.text: No. Step 3 is optional and blocks no run. A run that only needs sequencing verdicts goes from step 2 straight to step 4. See Step 3. Cell stock preparation.

docs.title: Why is a clone missing from the step 3 export?
docs.text: Only PASS clones ship. The Excluded list on step 3 gives the reason for each clone left out, for example an AMBIGUOUS or LOWDEPTH verdict.

docs.title: Step 4 blocks the export with a label mismatch
docs.text: A confirmation mean differs notably from the primary value of the same variant, which can mean a label swap. Check the plate layout and the verdict labels. If they're right, tick Allow reviewed label mismatch and build again. See Step 4. Activity Data.

docs.title: Why are some variants missing from the EVOLVEpro file?
docs.text:
Only variants with an explicit Pass verdict, no failure or fallback replicate mark and no conflict between duplicate rows are written. The build result reports how many were excluded by the NGS verdict. If none pass, the build fails instead of writing an empty file.

→ KURO overview | MAME overview

docs.title: Step 1. Load Variants
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Missing information

Numbered marks: 2 Browse; 3 Target Gene; 4 Organism

Numbered marks: 5 Compute from a genome

Numbered marks: 6 Import a table file

Load the sequence file the design is built on, then set the gene to design primers for and the codon usage table to use.

docs.title: What you do here
docs.text:
1. Press Browse, or drag a file into the window, to load the sequence.
  2. Pick the target CDS under Target Gene. The longest coding sequence is selected first, so a single-gene file needs no change.
  3. Pick Organism, which selects the codon usage table. The table decides which codon is written at each mutation site: of the codons for the new amino acid, those the organism hardly uses are left out and the frequently used ones are preferred, so even the mutated codon is optimised for the expression host. It is set automatically when the sequence annotation names an organism. Add organism..., the last entry of that list, installs a table for an organism kuma does not ship.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Item Accepted format Sequence File GenBank .gb, .gbk, .gbff, or SnapGene .dna Target Gene One of the CDS entries found in the loaded file Organism One of the nine built-in codon usage tables, or one you installed yourself

Once a file is loaded, the sequence header, the length in bp, and the number of genes found appear under the file name.

Only the first GenBank record and its CDS features are loaded. To use a gene from another record, export that record with its flanking template as a separate GenBank file. A later record's annotations cannot substitute for missing CDS annotations in the first record.

docs.title: Using your own strain
docs.text:
The nine bundled tables are E. coli, B. subtilis, H. sapiens, S. cerevisiae, K. phaffii (GS115, the organism most protocols still call P. pastoris), C. griseus (the CHO line), C. glutamicum, A. niger, P. putida. A table for any other organism is installed once and stays available. There are three ways to install one, and each of them puts the organism in this list.

Add organism... opens a dialog with two ways to build the table. Compute from a genome takes a GenBank file (.gb, .gbk, .gbff) or a CDS FASTA and counts the codons itself, then reports how many coding sequences it counted and which it left out before anything is installed. Import a table file takes a table you already have, as a kuma table (JSON), a three-column CSV, EMBOSS cusp output, or a Kazusa codon usage page pasted as text.

The third way needs no dialog: put the .json file in the codon table folder and press Refresh under Settings, Codon tables. That panel shows the folder path, and the folder holds a TEMPLATE.json.txt to copy and a README.txt describing the format. The file name without .json becomes the organism name kuma records, so ecoli_lab.json becomes ecoli_lab.

Whichever way is used, the table is checked before it is installed, and a file that fails a check is listed with the reason rather than half-loaded. A table cannot take the name of a built-in one, so a modified copy goes in under a name such as ecoli_lab.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text: Message What it means and what to do No file selected (.gb / .dna) No sequence yet. Press Browse and pick a file. CDS annotation required. Use a GenBank (.gb/.gbk) or SnapGene (.dna) file. A FASTA file was picked. FASTA carries no CDS annotation, so it cannot drive a design. Use a GenBank or SnapGene file. Load a sequence file first Shown in place of the gene list. Load the file first. UniProt BLAST search in progress… (Step 2 available after) A UniProt search is running on the loaded sequence. Wait for it to finish. Sequence file is required An entry in the Missing information dialog raised by Next. Load a sequence, then press Next again.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 2. Mutations

docs.title: Step 2. Mutations
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Set EVOLVEpro round

Numbered marks: 2 Browse; 3 Round and Size under Campaign round

Numbered marks: 4 Mutation column; 5 Ranking column

Numbered marks: 6 Selection mode; 7 Candidate table

Load an EVOLVEpro prediction table and choose the variants that go into this design.

docs.title: What you do here
docs.text:
1. Press Browse and pick the prediction file. .csv, .tsv, .xlsx, and .xls are accepted.
  2. Check Round and Size under Campaign round. Later steps derive their defaults from these.
  3. Confirm Mutation column and Ranking column under Column mapping. Auto-detect is the default.
  4. Pick Top-N only or Pipeline under Selection mode.
  5. Tick and untick rows in the candidate table to settle the final list.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
Display How to read it {n} variants loaded Total variants read from the file. Top-N only (y_pred descending) Takes the highest-scoring rows from the top down. Pipeline (step-by-step filtering) Selects through the pool filters in Step 4. Extra candidates shown How many unselected candidates to add to the table. 0 shows only the selected ones. {n} mutations entered Variants going into the design, followed by ({n} validated) and ({n} failed).

Failed lines are listed below the table with their line number, the raw text, and the reason.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text: Message What it means and what to do No file selected No prediction file yet. Press Browse and pick one. Round history suggests round N, but this is set to M. The saved round history disagrees with the round number entered. Correct the number, or leave it if it is intended. EVOLVEpro file load failed: … Auto-detect did not work, or a chosen column is not in this file. The message lists the headers found. Pick the mutation and ranking columns yourself, then press Apply selected columns. No columns detected in this file. Check the file, or pick another sheet. Choose a different sheet in the xlsx, or check the file. Top-N ranges from 1 to 96. Increase it to load more variants from CSV. The value it refers to is Design count: on Step 3. One design run covers one plate worth of variants. All {n} additional candidates shown No further candidates remain to display. Mutation input is required An entry in the Missing information dialog raised by Next. Load a prediction file first.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 3. Primer Parameters

docs.title: Step 3. Primer Parameters
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Strategy:; 2 Polymerase:; 3 Design count:

Numbered marks: 4 Advanced options

Numbered marks: 5 Fwd:; 6 Rev:; 7 Overlap:; 8 Tm tol ±

Numbered marks: 9 Range:; 10 Limit; 11 Auto-rescue failed mutations

Numbered marks: 12 Seed:

Numbered marks: 13 Custom Polymerase

Choose the design strategy and the polymerase, and set how many candidates this run designs. The remaining values work at their defaults.

docs.title: Main settings
docs.text:
Item What you choose Strategy: Partial overlap (Gibson) designs forward and reverse independently with the overlap upstream of the codon. Full overlap (Q5 SDM) makes the reverse the reverse-complement of the forward, so one pair covers the mutation site. Polymerase: Picking a preset also sets the recommended annealing temperature rule, the GC range, and the overlap mode. The default is KOD. Custom Polymerase lets you define your own. Design count: How many variants this run designs. The plate count is shown beside it.

Changing the polymerase overwrites the Tm targets and the GC range with that preset's values, so re-check them if you set them by hand. The 7 built-in presets carry the same Tm and GC values, so switching between built-ins leaves the numbers on screen unchanged.

Design-time Tm uses the fixed SantaLucia 1998 formula. The formula does not change when the polymerase changes.

docs.title: Advanced options
docs.text:
Expand Advanced options for the values below.

Item Default Tm (Fwd: Rev: Overlap:) 62 °C, 58 °C, 42 °C. Full overlap collapses these into a single Primer: field. Tm tol ± 4.0 °C. 2 to 5 °C is recommended. GC% Range: 40 to 60 %. Primer Length Limit On, with F at 18 to 39 bp and R at 19 to 27 bp. Turning it off uses the length bounds of the selected polymerase preset. Auto-rescue failed mutations On. Runs a retry pass with relaxed constraints. Seed: Empty. A value is recorded with the design only and does not change primer ranking. Strict off-target check Off. When on, a candidate is also dropped when any stretch of 15 bases or more of either primer matches the template exactly outside its intended site, on either strand, whether or not the 3' end could extend there. It is stricter than the default rules. A mutation that loses every candidate only to this check says so in its failure reason, and turning the check off recovers it.

The default off-target rules also look at sites that cross the origin of a circular template and at partial sites past the end of a linear sequence. A template counts as circular when its file declares it, as GenBank and SnapGene files do; a plain FASTA is read as linear.

After you leave a number field, it shows the value that was actually stored. An empty or non-numeric entry returns to the default, and a field that limits its range (for example Tm tol ±, capped at 10) shows the limited value.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text: Message What it means and what to do Design count limited to one plate of variants A value above 96 was entered. One run covers one plate, so the count is set back to 96. CSV contains only {n} variants The design count is larger than the number of variants loaded. Lower the count, or load more variants. Min must be less than Max A GC or length range is reversed. Correct the two values.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 4. Pool Filters & Run

docs.title: Step 4. Pool Filters & Run
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Design summary (Top-N)

Numbered marks: 2 Run Design

Numbered marks: 3 Design summary (Pipeline (failover))

Numbered marks: 4 Pool filters, the Pipeline steps

Numbered marks: 5 Pre-flight check (warnings)

The screen right before the design job starts. Check the inputs collected so far, then run primer design.

docs.title: Design summary
docs.text:
The card at the top shows the values this run will use. If something is not what you expect, go back to the earlier step and fix it there.

Item What it shows Sequence Name and length of the loaded sequence. Not loaded when there is none Mutation source Where the variants came from. An EVOLVEpro table reads evolvepro Selection mode Pipeline (failover) or Top-N only Variants Number of variants this run will design Polymerase Chosen polymerase, target Tm, primer cap

docs.title: What Pipeline mode adds
docs.text:
When step 2 is set to Pipeline, a PIPELINE box sits below the summary card. With Top-N only the box is absent and the screen shows only the summary card and Run Design.

The steps in the box apply from top to bottom. The checkbox in front of each step name turns it on or off.

On screen What it does Step 1: Pre-filter Caps how many variants one residue position can contribute. When two scores are within 2 %, it keeps the gentler amino-acid change (smaller Grantham distance) Step 2: Domain allocation Splits the picks among domains. Linker handling and the domain list are set here Step 3: Optimization Puts variants far from those already picked first, using 3D distance when a structure is loaded and sequence distance otherwise Step 4: Structural diversity Spreads the picks evenly through the 3D structure across the whole pool, anchored on variants measured in earlier rounds

Whatever is set here is listed under Pipeline in the design report on the next step.

docs.title: Running the design
docs.text:
1. Click Run Design. The button in the middle of the page and the one in the footer do the same thing.
  2. Above 1,000 selected variants an input size warning appears with a time estimate. Choose whether to continue.
  3. Read the pre-flight dialog when it appears. With no errors listed, Continue with warnings proceeds.
  4. A progress bar is shown. Click Cancel to stop the run.
  5. As soon as the run produces any result, the app moves to the Output screen on its own.

A failed or cancelled run leaves you on this screen. Read the status message, fix the input or the parameters, then run again.

docs.title: Warnings and errors
docs.text: What you see What to do Yellow list above the button (Sequence file (Browse a .gb / .fasta / .dna file), Mutations (enter at least one mutation in the Mutation panel), Target gene (select one in the Sequence panel)) Go to the panel each line names and fill the value in. The button stays disabled until they are all present Pre-flight check failed For Sidecar is not ready, use the Retry button in the status bar or restart the app Pre-flight check (warnings) Advisory only, such as checking free disk space. You can continue after reading it

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 5. Summary

docs.title: Step 5. Summary
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Statistics line and result table; 2 Plate map

Numbered marks: 3 Candidate 3D structure analysis

Numbered marks: 4 3D structure view

Review the design output as a table and a plate map. This is where you decide which variants actually get exported.

docs.title: Screen layout
docs.text:
The left side holds a statistics line, the result table, and the 3D structure analysis below it. The right side holds the plate map. Drag the vertical handle in the middle to change the split. The button at the top right collapses the plate map and restores it.

Statistic Meaning Primers Primers that were designed successfully Plates 96-well plates the forward primers occupy Failed Variants no primer could be designed for Rescued Variants recovered by relaxing constraints or moving to an alternative position

docs.title: Result table
docs.text:
• Every column sorts. The sort order carries through to the plate map and to the export files.
  • The Include checkbox decides the fate of a row. Clear it and the row drops out of the plate map and out of every export file.
  • Click a failed row to open the retry popover. Suggested Tm and GC values are pre-filled.
  • When Pipeline + Fill on failure substituted these positions; retry is unnecessary. appears, another variant already took that slot and the retry button stays disabled.

docs.title: Plate map
docs.text: Plate pair review shows one forward plate together with its deduplicated reverse partner on the same page. A Shared reverse marker means several forward primers use the same reverse primer.

docs.title: 3D structure analysis
docs.text:
The Candidate 3D structure analysis panel below the table places the candidate positions on the protein structure.

  • With a UniProt accession it loads the AlphaFold structure. Without one it predicts from sequence with ESMFold, and the Active site and Binding site overlays are hidden in that case.
  • A sequence longer than 400 residues with no accession is not predicted. Provide an accession or load a file with Upload PDB/CIF.
  • Variant positions are spheres coloured by y_pred. Orange sticks are catalytic residues (Active site) and magenta spheres are ligand, substrate, or metal binding residues (Binding site). These are not protein-protein interfaces.
  • Click a row in Color legend to show or hide that layer in the 3D view.
  • Structural Dispersion compares how clustered or spread the chosen positions are against random residue sets. P1 means strongly clustered and P99 means strongly spread.

Treat this panel as an interpretation and QC aid. It does not filter candidates.

docs.title: When the table is empty
docs.text: On-screen text What to do No results yet No design run has happened yet. Go back to Step 4 and run one This workspace has no primer results A design input changed after the run, so the primer output was discarded. Check the time and counts in the message, then run again

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 6. Export

docs.title: Step 6. Export
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Export name; 2 Forward primer plate name

Numbered marks: 3 Reverse primer plate name; 4 Amount (0.05 or 0.2 μmole)

Numbered marks: 5 Echo transfer volume; 6 Echo source plate columns

Numbered marks: 7 JANUS transfer volume

Numbered marks: 8 Export All

Numbered marks: 9 Echo and JANUS mapping preview

Numbered marks: 10 Order summary

Save the design output as order files and instrument transfer files in one batch.

Select the files to export: the Macrogen order sheet (forward and reverse primers together), primer FASTA, Echo, and JANUS. Macrogen, FASTA and Echo are selected by default; JANUS is not. The plate map for MAME and the run manifest are always included. Clearing every checkbox exports just those two files. The selection is saved with the project and applies to every round.

docs.title: Fields to fill
docs.text:
1. Export name sets the folder name and the file prefix. Leave it empty for an automatic kuro_YYMMDD_HHMM name. Up to 40 letters, numbers, Korean characters, underscores, or hyphens.
  2. Forward primer plate name and Reverse primer plate name take 1-20 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens. Both are required when the Macrogen order sheet is selected.
  3. Order vendor is fixed to Macrogen Plate Oligo. Choose 0.05 or 0.2 μmole for the amount. Purification is fixed to MOPC.
  4. Echo transfer volume accepts 25-500 nL.
  5. Echo source plate columns is where a 96-head starts stamping the 384 plate. Forward primers start there and reverse primers go to the paired quadrant. Name the quadrants already spent on the plate and an overlapping choice is refused.
  6. JANUS transfer volume accepts 0.5-10 μL.
  7. Click Export, then choose the destination folder. With a project open, the picker starts in the design folder of that project. Designs exceeding 96 wells export one round at a time.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
A folder named <Export name>_YYYYMMDD is created inside the folder you chose, or kuro_YYMMDD_HHMM when the name was left empty. An existing name gets _2 appended. Only selected files and the two mandatory files are written, all with that folder name as their prefix. Echo source plate choices are required only when Echo is selected.

File When you use it ..._macrogen.xls Attach it as is when ordering primer synthesis from Macrogen ..._primers.fasta Open it to feed the primer sequences into another tool or to read them ..._echo.csv The transfer list you load onto the Echo ..._echo.xlsx The same Echo transfer list in a form a person can review ..._janus.csv The transfer list you load onto the JANUS ..._janus.xlsx The same JANUS transfer list in a form a person can review ..._platemap.xlsx Open it at the bench to see which variant sits in which well ..._run.json The record of this export: its inputs and the plate layout. Open it later to check what the run was made with

docs.title: Preview and order summary
docs.text: The Echo and JANUS tabs under the form show the layout that will be stamped before you save anything. Order summary at the bottom lists plates, total primers, and mutations.

docs.title: Warnings and errors
docs.text: What you see What to do A warning toast about missing required input Fill in the items it lists. The two plate names are the usual cause wells exceed one 96-well plate. Clear Include on rows in the result table until 96 or fewer remain. The button stays disabled until then Use 1-20 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens. Remove spaces and symbols from the plate name Use up to 40 letters, numbers, Korean characters, underscores, or hyphens. Shorten the export name or replace the characters it rejects A partial success notice It names the files that failed. Open the folder, check what landed, then export again

docs.title: Next
docs.text: KURO work ends here. When the sequencing data come back, go to the MAME tab of the same project folder.

docs.title: KURO 6-step workflow
docs.text: KURO is a 6-step wizard that designs primers and exports the order files. Every step screen carries a Step N: Title heading at the top and Back and Next buttons at the bottom.

docs.title: The six steps
docs.text: Step Screen name What it does 1 Load Variants Load a sequence file and set the target gene and organism. Details 2 Mutations Load a prediction table and choose the variants to design. Details 3 Primer Parameters Set the strategy, polymerase, design count, and Tm/GC ranges. Details 4 Pool Filters & Run Check the summary and press Run Design. Details 5 Summary Read the result table, the plate map, and the report. Details 6 Export Save the order files and the instrument files. Details

docs.title: Moving between steps
docs.text:
Click any step in the list on the left to go there directly.

Next checks the required input for that step. When something is missing, a Missing information dialog opens and names what is absent. Clicking a step in the left list does not run this check.

The Sequence Map at the top of the window stays visible on every step. It reads No sequence loaded until a sequence is loaded.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: → Step 1. Load Variants

docs.title: Step 1. Barcode Setup
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Input files

Numbered marks: 2 Gene coordinates; 3 Gene name; 4 Polymerase; 5 Advanced options

Numbered marks: 6 Output location; 7 Generate Barcode Package

This screen builds a MAME barcode package from a CDS sequence and a barcode seed file. The amplicon reference and the barcode table it writes become the input of the step 2 analysis.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
1. In Input files, choose the CDS sequence and the barcode seeds xlsx.
  2. Check Gene coordinates. When a CDS candidate is found in the file, it appears in a dropdown and fills the coordinates for you.
  3. In Project metadata, enter the gene name and pick a polymerase.
  4. Open Advanced options if the overhang or binding parameters need changing.
  5. Choose an Output location. Leave it empty and the files go to the design/ folder of the project.
  6. Press Generate Barcode Package.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Format Required CDS sequence .fa .fasta .gb .gbk .dna Required Barcode Seeds xlsx .xlsx holding the fwd_1..12 and rev_1..8 seed sequences Required Gene coordinates gene_start, gene_end (0-based, end exclusive) Required Gene name Short identifier used in the output filenames Required Polymerase Q5 / Taq / Phusion / KOD Defaults to Q5 Output location Folder Optional

The CDS sequence must be a plasmid or construct map that carries flanking template on both sides of the gene. MAME primers bind outside the gene and never inside it, so each side needs at least as much template as the smallest usable overhang, which is the larger of overhang_min and binding_min_len (20 bp per side at the defaults), not the full overhang_max. On a linear template the reach is clamped to the sequence ends, and a circular template wraps around the origin, so the requirement applies to linear templates only. A CDS-only FASTA will not work.

The two search parameters both measure overhang: how far the outer end of the amplicon reaches past the CDS boundary. That is the same distance trim_flank_bp and the terminal variant advisories use. The gap between a primer and the gene is not configurable and is always zero or more, because a base a primer covers is read from the primer rather than from the template. Since overhang equals that gap plus the binding length, an overhang_min below binding_min_len describes a range no primer can occupy and is reported as a warning. The default search bounds are 20 and 60.

For GenBank input, only the first record and its CDS annotations are loaded. Export a desired later record with its flanking template as a separate GenBank file; annotations from different records cannot be combined with the first template.

The Template topology choice appears only for a plain FASTA (.fa, .fasta), because a FASTA records no topology. A GenBank or SnapGene file carries its own topology, so the choice stays hidden for those.

docs.title: Primer quality checks
docs.text:
A barcode primer binding site has to clear the same five criteria a KURO SDM primer does before it is selected: the Tm window (55-68 C by default), the 3' terminal GC clamp, hairpin, homodimer and off-target binding. Hairpin and homodimer are rejected when the primer3 structure Tm exceeds 40.0 C. Off-target scans the whole template that was loaded and rejects a candidate when any site outside the intended binding position binds at 45.0 C or above. The thresholds match the KURO defaults and are not exposed on screen. Hairpin and homodimer use fixed design-scale concentrations rather than the polymerase profile, so changing the enzyme cannot change which molecule gets ordered. The Tm window keeps following the polymerase profile as before.

The off-target search space is whatever file was loaded. A plasmid or construct map that carries the flanking sequence is searched the way KURO searches a template; a FASTA holding the CDS alone offers that much less sequence to search.

When no candidate clears all five, the design is not refused. The candidate whose Tm is closest to the target is selected instead and a warning states which check it failed and at what temperature. Read that warning before ordering the primers.

The molecules that are actually synthesised are the 20 oligos formed by a seed joined to a binding site. Hairpin and homodimer are run over those full oligos too, and everything above 40.0 C is collected into a single warning. That pass is advisory and never changes the binding site it chose: kuma only chooses binding sites, and each barcode seed is a fixed input sequence from the seeds file, so the program has no other seed to swap in. Check the full sequence of every oligo the warning names before ordering. To move a binding site elsewhere, change the search range or the binding length under Advanced options and generate again. An oligo longer than 60 nt is reported as unchecked, since primer3 refuses the calculation at that length.

docs.title: Warnings and errors
docs.text:
What the screen says What to do Could not read gene annotations from this file Check whether the GenBank or SnapGene file is damaged, then pick another file No CDS detected. Enter coordinates manually. Type gene_start and gene_end yourself gene_end must be greater than gene_start. Check that the two coordinates are not swapped Primer design may fail on a linear template Template outside the gene is shorter than the smallest usable overhang. Lower binding length or overhang_min, or use a file with longer flanking sequence. The button stays usable A project must be open to generate a package Choose Open Project from the File menu. With no project the button stays disabled Cannot proceed, missing required input Fill in the items listed in the toast. The button is clickable even with empty fields and answers with this notice Generation failed Read the reason in the notice. Pressing again without changing a parameter gives the same outcome

When the output folder already exists, a confirmation asks before anything is overwritten.

docs.title: Generated files
docs.text:
On success, Generated files lists three entries.

  • Barcode table (xlsx)
  • Amplicon reference (FASTA)
  • Run context (JSON)

Open folder opens the save location. Once generation finishes, the amplicon reference becomes the step 2 reference and the barcode table becomes the custom barcode file automatically. Pressing Next before the package exists blocks the move.

→ Step 2. Sequencing Review

docs.title: Step 2. Sequencing Review
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 MinKNOW run folder; 2 Expected variants (xlsx)

Numbered marks: 3 Reference construct

Numbered marks: 4 Wells used; 5 Run

Numbered marks: 6 Verdict table; 7 96-well plate map

Score the sequencing run well by well and read the outcome on a 96-well plate. Pick the inputs in 2.1 and read the verdicts in 2.2.

docs.title: 2.1 Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required MinKNOW run folder Required Expected variants (xlsx) Required Reference construct Required Wells used Optional. Left untouched, the leading wells are used

Choose the inputs, then press Run or Validate. Cell stock preparation is not on this screen. It is step 3.

docs.title: What MAME reads in the run folder
docs.text:
Give the folder MinKNOW wrote, as it is. Sorting reads into barcode folders beforehand isn't needed.

File Used for Required *.fastq or *.fastq.gz in the barcode folders under fastq_pass/ The reads analyzed Required final_summary_*.txt, sample_sheet_*.csv Run name and sample information Read if present sequencing_summary*.txt or *.tsv Read quality and barcode cross-talk check Read if present pore_activity_*.csv, throughput_*.csv, barcode_alignment*.tsv Run health indicators Read if present report_*.json Flow cell type and pore counts Read if present

Compression doesn't matter. Both *.fastq and *.fastq.gz are read.

If report_*.json isn't in the run folder, MAME looks one level up. When it's absent altogether the pore fields stay blank. Blank is not zero.

pod5/, fast5/, bam_pass/, other_reports/ and report_*.html are never read. Leaving them in place changes nothing.

docs.title: Wells used
docs.text:
The "Wells used" panel draws the computed placement on a plate. Each mutation is fixed to the well that plate order (A1, B1, ... H1, A2) gave it, and clicking a well never moves anything. The selection only states which wells this campaign actually filled.

A well that is not selected is a well the campaign did not fill, so it is not scored. The sample that had been placed there is named in 2.2. Selecting fewer wells than samples is simply a partly filled plate and not a reason for refusal. The only selection refused is an empty one.

The Barcode worklist (csv) button in the same panel saves a file with one row per filled well carrying the well, the sample, the barcode token and the seed primer names. Use it at the bench when pipetting.

docs.title: Advanced options
docs.text:
Four settings sit under Advanced options in the parameter panel.

On screen Default What it changes Coverage Fraction 0.98 How much of the reference one read must cover to pass. Raise it to keep only complete alignments, lower it to admit partial ones Minimum mapping quality (0–60) 25 Reads mapped below this quality are discarded Edit Distance Ratio 0.25 How loosely a barcode may match. Smaller is stricter and assigns fewer reads Chimera Split on Counts a read spanning several wells as separate hits. Leave it on

The remaining verdict thresholds can't be changed from the screen.

docs.title: Changing an input clears the previous output
docs.text: Changing the run folder, the expected variants workbook, the reference construct, the selected wells or an analysis parameter clears the verdicts and plate map the previous run produced, and 2.2 returns to its pre-run state. This keeps the screen of a finished run from looking like the outcome of the new inputs. Picking the same value again does nothing. The output path is not an input, so it clears nothing.

docs.title: What a run does
docs.text:
The stages below are the path for a MinKNOW run folder. The other two modes take a folder of FASTA files that already exist and skip the earlier stages. From stage 2 on, the progress bar shows these names.

  1. Amplicon extraction. MAME locates where the barcode workbook primers sit in the reference and cuts out the region between them to align against. If it can't locate them, it uses the reference as supplied.
  2. Aligning. The bundled minimap2 maps the reads in fastq_pass onto the reference.
  3. Coverage filter. Reads with low mapping quality, and reads that don't cover enough of the reference, are dropped.
  4. Demultiplexing. The barcodes at both ends of each surviving read assign it to one of 96 wells. A read whose barcode on either side can't be resolved, or ties, is dropped.
  5. Building consensus. For each well the bases at each position are pooled into one sequence by majority vote. Low-quality bases are left out of the vote and positions with too few reads are left as N.
  6. Analyzing. Each well sequence is compared against the expected mutation and given a verdict.

docs.title: What a run writes
docs.text:
• Per-well consensus sequences, written as {R}_{F}.fasta under the barcode folder (sort_barcodeNN/) of the output folder.
  • final/consensus_all_dna.fasta, all wells merged.
  • The verdict table and plate view on screen.
  • The picked clone list ..._picks.csv.
  • The Excel workbook, written to the output path chosen for the run.

Use a separate output folder for each run. Plate folders an earlier run left behind are excluded from the verdicts and named on screen.

docs.title: 2.2 Review
docs.text: The verdict table sits on the left. The 96-well plate map and the per-plate verdict bar sit on the right. The tabs above the verdict table are Final, ALL, and the native barcodes actually present in this run. Final keeps only the well of the selected replicate for each mutation.

docs.title: Notices above the verdict table
docs.text:
Each notice checks the run that just finished and appears only when its condition holds. Several can appear together, and none appears when there's nothing to report. Notices from an earlier run don't pile up: changing an input clears them with the previous result, and running again decides them afresh from the new result.

  • This run cannot be scored The median reads per well is under the floor. The verdicts below come from a plate that never had the depth to be read, so sequence the plate again rather than using them.
  • This run is scorable but under-powered Depth clears the floor and falls short of the recommendation. Use the verdicts and check borderline wells separately. Depth is measured only over the wells this run actually scored.
  • Mutations at a reference end When the codon of an expected mutation sits near an end of the reference, that mutation is named. An aligner clips reads at that point, so the position can be read shallower than the depth the well reports. Re-run with a reference that includes the region where the primers bind.
  • N samples are not on this plate Names the samples and wells left out of the selection. Having no verdict for them in this run is expected. Include them in a later run if they are needed.
  • Well-variant mapping likely mismatched Observed mutations match other wells' expected mutations better than their own. It does not block the run. Check the correspondence between the plate you pipetted and the sample names before using the output. Below 24 wells with an observed mutation the sample is too small and no judgment is made.

The flow cell id and pore count appear in the same place. They are reference values and no pass line is set on them.

docs.title: Opening the evidence behind a verdict
docs.text:
• Replicate rows: the replicate list in the verdict detail is made of buttons. Pressing a row selects that plate replicate, and the detail, the plate highlight and the verdict table follow it.
  • Confidence metrics: pressing a metric name shows what the value counts, at which pipeline stage it is counted, and whether it can move the verdict. The threshold this run compared against is shown too. Seven of the ten metrics are diagnostic and change no verdict.
  • Verdict legend: hovering a class in the plate map legend or in the per-plate verdict bar shows what that class means, including classes with no wells.

docs.title: Verdict classes
docs.text:
A well gets its verdict from the checks below, in order, and the first one that holds decides. Moving on to the next check means no verdict yet, not a pass.

  1. Read count below the configured minimum: Low depth.
  2. Net consensus indel length not a multiple of 3: Frameshift.
  3. Indel signal at or above the threshold while every expected substitution matches: Ambiguous.
  4. Too high a fraction of N among the positions that can be judged: No call.
  5. No read count reported and the consensus file too small: Low depth.
  6. Two nucleotide indel markers close together within the frameshift window: Frameshift.
  7. More amino-acid changes than both the design count and the configured limit: Many.
  8. A mixed-allele signal remains: Mixed, or Low depth when the well's read count is below the confidence depth.
  9. An expected substitution missing or carrying the wrong amino acid: Wrong AA.
  10. An extra amino-acid change within the window around an expected site: Ambiguous.
  11. Any other extra amino-acid change: Wrong AA.

A well that meets none of these is Pass. Checks that are not configured or cannot run are skipped, so when a verdict looks wrong, open that well's details as well.

Verdict Meaning Pass Observed amino-acid changes exactly match the expected design Ambiguous All expected mutations matched, and either an extra AA change sits within the indel window of an expected site or the reads carry an indel-event signal at or above the threshold (this can mark a WT control too). Still counts as detected Mixed Within-well contamination: a substantial second allele in the consensus signal Wrong AA An expected site shows a different amino acid, an expected mutation is missing, or an unexpected extra change sits outside the window while none sits inside it Frameshift The consensus carries a net insertion or deletion whose length is not a multiple of 3, so the reading frame is shifted Many More observed AA changes than both the design and the many-mutation cutoff Low depth Too few reads to call this well reliably No call Consensus has too many ambiguous (N) positions to trust the amino-acid calls

Runs with no verdicts, heavy loss at the coverage filter and other common problems are answered in the FAQ.

→ Step 3. Cell stock preparation is optional. Stop here if only a sequencing verdict is needed.

→ Step 4. Activity Data filters activity measurements by these verdicts to build the EVOLVEpro input.

docs.title: Step 3. Cell stock preparation
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Destination layout; 2 Volume (µL); 3 Liquid class; 4 type column value

Numbered marks: 5 Preview

Numbered marks: 6 Excluded; 7 Output file path; 8 Export Janus Mapping

This screen turns the selected clones into the sheet the robot reads. It is optional and blocks no run. A run that only needs sequencing verdicts goes from step 2 straight to step 4.

The settings unfold on this page rather than in a dialog.

docs.title: The two files
docs.text:
File When it is written Content ..._picks.csv Automatically, when the step 2 analysis finishes The selected clone list ..._janus.csv Only when export is pressed on this screen The 8-column sheet the robot reads

A notice at the top of the screen reports what became of each file. The selection list is written by every run, while the instrument mapping is written only by a person exporting one.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
1. Pick a Destination layout. Source position keeps each destination well at the source plate position. Plate order from A1 fills down each column (A1, B1, C1 to H1, then A2), leaving no empty wells.
  2. In Instrument settings, enter Volume (µL), Liquid class and the type column value.
  3. Read the Preview for the rows that will be written and the generated plate names.
  4. Read Excluded for the clones left out and why.
  5. Choose an Output file path. The extension is fixed to .csv.
  6. Press Export Janus Mapping.

The 8 columns of the sheet are name, type, no, Asp. Rack, Asp. Posi, Dsp. Rack, Dsp. Posi, volume.

docs.title: Three things the preview can say
docs.text:
What the screen says Meaning Fix the problems below before exporting. The export button is locked. Fix the listed problems Written as noted below. None of this blocks the export. A list of values the program derived by itself. Read it and move on Preview unavailable Press Retry preview. Exporting stays available

With Source position selected, the export fails when two picks land on the same well.

docs.title: Excluded clones
docs.text:
Only PASS clones ship. AMBIGUOUS carries a side indel and LOWDEPTH is unverified, so both are listed as excluded. The reasons are grouped into five.

Reason Meaning Failed The verdict is a failure No plate selected That plate is not part of the current selection No verdict record The well has no verdict on record Verdict class not included The verdict is something other than PASS Fallback pick The pick was taken as a fallback candidate

docs.title: Liquid class and plate names
docs.text:
The liquid class drives the pipetting behaviour of the robot, so no default is assumed. The instrument sheet has no column for it, so it is recorded with the run and written to no file. Export proceeds even when the field is empty.

Asp. Rack and Dsp. Rack carry plate names generated from the plates of this run rather than deck numbers. Sources take Stock plate1, Stock plate2 in plate order, and the one destination is final culture plate. Read them back in the preview and label the deck to match.

docs.title: Completion mark
docs.text:
Step 3 is marked complete once a liquid class is entered or a mapping is exported. A successful export leaves the saved path on the screen.

→ Step 2. Sequencing Review | Step 4. Activity Data

docs.title: Step 4. Activity Data
docs.text:
Numbered marks: 1 Experiment data file; 2 Activity scale (raw or relative to WT)

Numbered marks: 3 Additional measurement format; 4 NGS verdict xlsx

Numbered marks: 5 Output EVOLVEpro xlsx; 6 Convert to EVOLVEpro input format

Numbered marks: 7 Add xlsx files (4.2 per-round EVOLVEpro results); 8 Run classification (4.2)

Filter this round's activity measurements by the NGS verdicts of the same round, then apply WT normalization and replicate merging to build the EVOLVEpro input xlsx. Build the file in 4.1 and read the direction for the next round in 4.2.

docs.title: 4.1 Convert to EVOLVEpro input format
docs.text:
1. Choose the Experiment data file. The format is read from the file contents, and csv, xlsx and xls are accepted.
  2. If one file reads as two formats, pick one. The screen states what separates them.
  3. If some variants were picked after the primary screen and measured again several times (a confirmation measurement), put that xlsx in Additional experiment data file (optional). The format is read from the file and Additional measurement format follows it. Pick the format there yourself when the screen asks, and always for a numeric-ID replicate report. Without a confirmation file it stays at None.
  4. Choose the NGS verdict xlsx. This is the verdict Analyze produced for this round, and it is required.
  5. Choose the Output EVOLVEpro xlsx path and press Convert to EVOLVEpro input format.

Everything after the format choice is the same. Normalization, replicate merging, the NGS verdict and the export form one pipeline.

docs.title: Measurement formats
docs.text:
Format Label Value Also needed Generic long-format Well or variant Activity scale selects raw or relative to WT A well-to-variant map when labels are wells GC data sheet Well Already relative to WT A well-to-variant map Raw Agilent report Well Normalized by the WT block mean in the report A well-to-variant map Numeric-ID Agilent report Plate position number Normalized by the WT block mean in the report A variant order reference

Well labels need a map saying which variant sits in each well. Given a Plate layout xlsx, that sheet is the map. Without it, the mapping comes from the variant names the NGS verdict sheet records for each well. A variant seated in two wells is refused, because the well to attach NGS evidence to cannot be settled as one.

For numeric IDs, number i means the i-th variant in plate order, so a file stating that order is needed. The designed variant list is used first, the plate layout when that is absent. An ID set that does not match the order one to one is refused rather than attached to neighboring variants.

A GC run is shared, so a report can carry rows that are not this run's: BLANK, internal standards, calibration standards named by concentration (1, 5, 10 in a well-labeled report), and other experiments' samples. Those rows are set aside, and each is named with its block and sheet row in the warnings and in the manifest excluded_rows, with a count per reason in exclusion_reason_counts. A row that names this run's own well or variant in the other notation (a variant name of this run in a well-labeled report, a well of this plate in a numeric-ID report) refuses the file, because one run's measurements are then split across two notations. A file with no row of this run is refused too. WT rows that repeat a replicate number, and a well measured twice in a one-replicate report, stay in the mean and are flagged in the warnings. A numeric ID is a position rather than a name, so an ID past the plate (or past the above-WT subset for a confirmation) says the file or the order is wrong, and it is refused rather than set aside.

docs.title: Generic long-format requirements
docs.text:
• Exactly one label column and exactly one value column.
  • Well labels and variant labels are not mixed in one file.
  • Raw values carry no negatives, NaN or infinity.
  • With raw selected, the mean of the WT rows of each plate_id is the denominator. Without a plate_id column, the whole file is one cohort.
  • With relative to WT selected, nothing is normalized again.

docs.title: Confirmation measurement (repeated re-measurement)
docs.text:
After the primary screen measures every well once, the variants worth a second look are collected and measured several times. This round exists to average repeated measurements, so the replicate mean replaces the primary value of the same variant. Give at most one of the three formats below.

  • Well / variant labels: a raw Agilent report with WT rows whose sample names are well labels (A1, A1-1) or variant labels (S11I, S11I-1).
  • Numeric-ID replicate report: the numbers count the subset that exceeded WT in the primary screen, not the whole plate. The order reference must be exactly one of the designed variant list or the plate layout. Giving both is refused.
  • Well-labeled replicate report: the sample names are wells with a replicate number, such as A1-1, A1-2, A1-3. Wells are mapped to variants the same way as in the primary measurement, and each area is divided by the mean of the WT well plus any WT rows, so the report needs no WT block. Sample names that are not well labels, such as other samples that shared the GC run, are set aside and named with their position in a warning.

The format is read from the file, per field: the same well-labeled report is the experiment data in the first field and a well-labeled confirmation in the additional field. A numeric-ID replicate report is never applied automatically, because its numbers count only the above-WT subset. If the format cannot be read, the screen says why and asks for it.

Inferring variant names from activity rank or from a previous EVOLVEpro file is no longer supported. A saved state pointing at that approach does not run and shows conversion guidance instead.

docs.title: What the NGS verdict filters out
docs.text: A variant is exported only when its verdict is an explicit Pass, carries no failure or fallback replicate mark, and has no verdict or variant identity conflict between duplicate rows. Rows with a missing verdict, a conflict, or anything other than Pass are excluded rather than presumed to pass. If no variant passes, the build fails rather than publishing an empty file as a success.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
The build result reports variants written, confirmation overrides, primary values and NGS-excluded counts. The output file carries exactly the two columns Variant and activity.

A confirmation mean that differs notably from the primary value is marked as a mismatch and blocks the export. Check the layout and the verdict labels, then release it with Allow reviewed label mismatch. Choosing an output path that another round already recorded as its output raises a notice that building here overwrites it.

When the measurement input, the verdict evidence or the output path changes, the previous completion mark becomes invalid and the file has to be built again.

docs.title: Positive clone JANUS mapping (optional)
docs.text:
This step below the 4.1 screen writes a JANUS worklist that moves the round-1 clones above wild-type from the final cell stock (96 PCR plate) to a 96 deep well plate (LB + Km). Find positive clones lists every measured clone, with the clones above wild-type ticked to start with. A value exactly equal to wild-type is left out. You can untick a clone or add one below wild-type, and the selection is kept with the project. The selected clones are placed from A1 of the target plate in the column order of their source wells (A1, B1 ... H1, A2). The file has the same eight columns as the step 3 sheet, and the volume (70 µL to start with) and both plate names are edited on screen. A long-format file has no source wells and cannot be used. This does not affect the EVOLVEpro input build.

Rows of the round-1 file that were set aside as not belonging to this run (blanks, calibration numbers, wells the mapping does not name, wild-type well readings not used as the reference) appear in the warning box above the checkboxes with their name, block and row, in the same sentences as the 4.1 build warnings. An empty, zero, negative or non-numeric volume disables the export and says why below the field.

docs.title: 4.2 Signals and handoff
docs.text:
Collect the per-round EVOLVEpro result xlsx files and run the advisory classification. The list is prefilled with the outputs 4.1 produced, and entries can be added or removed. Run classification answers with one of continue single-mutant walking, switch to combinatorial, stop, or defer, together with its reasons. The advice is read-only and confirms or saves nothing.

→ FAQ answers the label mismatch and missing variant questions.

→ MAME overview

docs.title: MAME workflow
docs.text: MAME runs in four steps, from barcode primer design through sequencing verdicts and the robot picking sheet to activity data. Click any step in the left rail to go straight there.

docs.title: The four steps
docs.text:
Step What the screen does 1. Custom Barcode Primer Design Builds a barcode package from a CDS sequence and a barcode seeds xlsx 2. Sequencing QC Analyzes a MinKNOW run folder and produces a verdict per well 3. Cell stock preparation Exports the selected clones as the sheet the robot reads 4. Activity Data Turns activity measurements into an EVOLVEpro input

The rail numbers a sub-step under each step. There are six: 1.1 Barcode Package, 2.1 Inputs, 2.2 Review, 3.1 Cell stock preparation, 4.1 Activity Data, 4.2 Signals and Handoff.

docs.title: Step 3 is optional
docs.text: A run that only needs sequencing verdicts goes from step 2 straight to step 4. No Janus value gates a run, step 2 or step 4. An analyze run writes the selection list (..._picks.csv) on its own, while the sheet the robot reads (..._janus.csv) is written only when export is pressed in step 3.

docs.title: The input is a MinKNOW run folder
docs.text: Step 2 takes the run folder MinKNOW wrote, as it is. Sorting it into barcode directories beforehand is not needed. MAME reads the .fastq and .fastq.gz files under fastq_pass/, aligns the reads to the reference, splits the barcodes, builds a consensus per well and scores it against the expected mutation. The files it reads, the adjustable values and each stage are in Analyze and review.
